NutriCorp Foods - Q3 2024 Earnings Call Transcript

Operator:
Good morning, and welcome to the NutriCorp Foods Q3 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are in a listen-only mode. After the speakers' presentation, there will be a question-and-answer session. To ask a question, you will need to register by pressing star one one. As a reminder, this conference is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the call over to Alex Rivera, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Alex Rivera (Head of Investor Relations):
Thank you, operator. Good morning, everyone, and thank you for joining us today to discuss NutriCorp Foods' Q3 2024 results. Joining me on the call are Johnathan Hale, Chief Executive Officer; Sarah Jenkins, Chief Financial Officer; Mike Thornton, Chief Growth Officer; and Lisa Chen, Chief Supply Chain Officer.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that this call may contain forward-looking statements. Please refer to our SEC filings for a discussion of the factors that could cause actual results to differ materially from these statements.

With that, I'll turn the call over to Johnathan Hale.

Johnathan Hale (CEO):
Thank you, Alex, and good morning, everyone. We are pleased to report our results for Q3 2024. We delivered strong performance despite ongoing macroeconomic headwinds and inflationary pressures.

Today, I'll be focusing on eight key areas: key achievements and challenges in the quarter, organic sales growth guidance for the next quarter and year, overall company performance highlights, performance of key brands and product categories, EPS guidance and key assumptions, organic revenue growth overall and by region, progress on sustainability initiatives and goals, and performance in key channels including retail, foodservice, and convenience.

First, regarding key achievements and challenges in the quarter. Our results reflect resilient execution in a volatile macro environment, with organic net sales growth of 7.2% year-over-year, powered by volume expansion and pricing actions against persistent inflation. Adjusted EBITDA margins expanded 120 basis points to 18.4%, highlighting our disciplined cost controls. Volume growth accelerated across core categories from prior softness. Total beverage volumes increased 4.1% year-over-year, spearheaded by our premium hydration segment where NutriFlow, our electrolyte-infused low-sugar functional water, achieved 12% volume growth and captured 1.2 share points in the U.S. convenience channel according to Nielsen data—a trend aligning with industry shifts toward health-focused ready-to-drink beverages like BodyArmor in PepsiCo's lineup. In snacks, our plant-based protein bars rebranded as VitaCrunch delivered 9.5% volume uplift, boosted by e-commerce which now makes up 15% of segment sales, rising from 11% last year.

In regions, APAC stood out, accounting for 28% of group revenues with 11.4% organic growth. Our partnership with Alibaba's Freshippo in China propelled double-digit distribution for ready-to-drink teas, while India benefited from strong demand for affordable hydration packs during monsoon season. Latin America grew 8.7% in Brazil and Mexico, where localized products like mango-chili sparkling water outperformed category growth by 300 basis points per Euromonitor. Operationally, our Supply Chain Resilience 2.0 initiative generated $45 million in savings through yield optimization in cocoa and sugar procurement. We've secured 85% of fiscal 2025 commodity needs at favorable rates, countering 15-20% year-over-year input cost inflation affecting peers such as Hershey and Mondelez. AI-driven demand forecasting with SAP's planning suite cut inventory by 18% and raised on-time delivery to 97%. On sustainability, 65% of palm oil is now RSPO-compliant ahead of EU deforestation rules, and we've introduced recyclable PET bottles for core sodas, improving brand Net Promoter Scores by 8 points among millennials.

Premiumization proved effective, with 42% of incremental sales from higher-margin SKUs and average revenue per unit up 3.2%. Our M&A advanced with the $250 million acquisition of Thai herbal beverage maker ZenLeaf, adding 2% to pro forma EPS in year one and strengthening APAC functional drinks against Suntory and locals.

Challenges persisted. North America, 55% of revenues, managed only 3.8% organic growth amid 4.1% core CPI inflation, with snack volumes down 1.2% as consumers traded down to private labels like at Kraft Heinz. Pricing offset this but trade spend rose to 14% of sales to protect space against Frito-Lay promotions. Input volatility hit hard: cocoa surged 45% quarter-over-quarter from West African shortages, costing chocolate-coated snacks 80 basis points in margin and $12 million in unhedged COGS. Freight, down 5% from peaks, remains 22% above 2019 levels due to Red Sea issues rerouting APAC shipments. Consumer health shifts challenged mix: low/no-sugar reformulations in 70% of beverages built loyalty but softened legacy carbonated soft drink volumes by 2.5%, similar to Coca-Cola's Zero Sugar path. In EMEA, 22% of sales, France's Nutri-Score mandates caused 4% volume drop in sweetened teas during formulation tweaks. Currencies shaved 1.9% off reported growth, with Argentine peso and Turkish lira depreciation leading; FX-neutral organic growth hit 9.1%. These affirm our Health Forward, Globally Powered strategy: R&D doubles to $180 million yearly for biotech sweeteners and upcycled ingredients, aiming for 20% portfolio innovation by fiscal 2026. We'll prune $100 million in low-margin SKUs next year, like Campbell's snack moves. Q4 guidance: organic sales plus 6-8%, EBITDA margins up 100 basis points year-over-year. We're set to gain share in the $1.2 trillion F&B market at 4.5% CAGR per Statista via premium, functional, sustainable trends.

Second, concerning organic sales growth guidance for the next quarter and year. Organic sales growth strips out acquisitions like PureBites organic snacks, FX, and divestitures such as non-core frozen meals. We've shown resilience amid 3.2% U.S. CPI and shifts to value, health, convenience. Q3 organic growth was 5.2%, with 2.1% volume, 2.8% pricing, 0.3% mix toward Health & Wellness at 28% of sales, up from 22% two years ago—beating PepsiCo's 4.1% and Mondelez's 4.8%. Snacks led at 7.1% via air-fried veggie crisps with 15% test market velocity and 85% ACV nationally.

For Q4, we guide 4% to 6% organic growth, seasonally softer lapping strong prior holiday and travel comps. Pricing: 2.5% to 3.0%, modest on snacks and beverages to cover cocoa/palm oil up 12% quarter-over-quarter; our 92% household penetration enables this like Kellogg's in cereals. Health & Wellness price/mix neutral to positive amid 8% category growth per Nielsen. Volume/mix: 1.5% to 3.0%, from innovations like zero-sugar electrolytes with fitness influencers for Gen Z (sports drinks up 11% YoY per IRI), low-cal RTD coffees for Starbucks-at-home, and 50% less sugar kids' snacks for UK HFSS rules. Distribution adds 1-2 points: e-commerce to 18% sales with 25% Amazon velocity post-Prime Day, Costco adding 500 doors for protein bars. North America (72% sales): 5-7%, snacks 9%; EMEA (15%): 2-4% offset by 12% plant-based dairy; APAC/LatAm (13%): 3-5%, Brazil refreshers and China Tmall snacking up 20%.

Full fiscal 2025: 5% to 7% organic, high end of 4-6% long-term, on FY24's 5.4% with 2.5-3% inflation. Portfolio optimization culls 15% low-velocity SKUs like Nestlé's power brands. Supply chain AI cuts stockouts to 2%, $150 million sustainable sourcing for 40% cocoa hedges volatility, appealing to 65% millennials per Kantar. Industry bifurcation: indulgence up 7%, staples to private label at 28% U.S. grocery; our Health & Wellness at 12% outpaces 4% average per Euromonitor, with Ozempic trends and QSR up 4% via McDonald's trials. Headwinds: U.S. tariffs 50 basis points cost, unemployment over 4.2%; but $1.2 billion productivity, 14% ROIC fund buybacks, M&A. Q4 4-6%, FY25 5-7% means profitable growth, 200 basis points gross margin expansion.

Third, in terms of overall company performance highlights. Consolidated net revenues hit $2.85 billion, up 8.2% year-over-year or 6.7% organic excluding FX/acquisitions—fifth straight double-digit organic in North American core. Volumes up 4.1%, strongest in three years, plus 2.6% net pricing. Adjusted EBITDA $512 million or 18.0% of sales, up 210 basis points on productivity and premium shift. Adjusted diluted EPS $1.12, up 14.3%, beating guidance.

Snacks & Confectionery (42% revenues, AuraCrunch nut bars, ZestBites chocolates) led at 10.5% organic, 5.8% volume, 120 basis points IRI share gain vs. 3.2% indulgent snacks. 30% reduced-sugar ZestBites hit 15% new trial. Beverages (35%, FrostQuench hydration, PureSip juices) 7.9% organic, 4.2% pricing offset summer volume softness; functional like FrostQuench Protein up 22% vs. Powerade. Nutrition & Convenience (23%, VitalBloom meals/yogurts) 4.8% organic, gaining on Nature Valley.

North America (68%) up 9.4%, club AUVs +6%; EMEA 5.2% despite inflation, Eastern dairy +8%; APAC 11.3%, China e-com +25%; LATAM 3.9% vs. FX via sorghum. Gross margins 38.4%, +160 basis points on $85 million productivity (70% procurement, 65% grains hedged 15% below spot), 12% SKU delist. SG&A 12.6% via digital trade tools cutting deductions 18%. Operating cash $420 million +22%, $250 million buybacks, dividend +12% to $0.42/share.

Leaning into premiumization (28% sales, 2x category), GreenHarvest regenerative ag 45% by FY25 cutting Scope 3 12%, AI demand sensing to 92% accuracy, inventory to 62 days. Five Q4 launches like zero-sugar FrostQuench RTD coffee for $15 billion energy adjacency. Q2 validates Thrive25: mid-single organic, 20%+ EBITDA, 15%+ ROIC by 2025. Raising FY guidance 7-9% organic, $2.15-$2.20 EPS amid normalizing costs, 3.5% grocery inflation.

Fourth, looking at performance of key brands and product categories. Segment net revenues grew 7.2% to $4.8 billion, 5.1% organic—2.8% volume/mix, 2.3% pricing—via revenue growth management with premiumization and EDLP amid inflation. Excluding 53rd week/FX 1.9%, share gains 110 basis points per Nielsen/IRI in e-com/convenience. Beverages (pillar): +6.8% organic to $2.1 billion on 3.1% ACV, 3.7% pricing. CSDs (45%) +4.2%, Zest Cola +11.5% volume, +1.2 share to 28.4% via Zest Zero Sugar (stevia, 15% SPINS trial). Non-carb +9.2% vs. 6.1% IRI, AquaPure alkaline +18% to 85% convenience ACV; VitalBoost Energy +22% volumes ($50B category 8% CAGR), TikTok influencers +7 points penetration. North America +8.1% on QSR/c-store +12%; EMEA +4.5% low-cal; APAC +14% China/India. AI dynamic pricing +1.2% uplift, 100% rPET Zest by Q4 (68% millennials eco per surveys).

Snacks & Confectionery +4.3% organic to $1.7 billion vs. flat IRI salty (+1.2%). CrunchMax tortilla #2 U.S. +5.6%, +80 bps to 14.2% on habanero relaunch (20% sales); NutriTrail nuts +12% keto appeal. Confectionery +2.1% despite 40% cocoa, FreshBurst gum +7% xylitol/oral health. LatAm +9.2% Mexico impulse; Europe +1.8% HFSS; North America +4%. 15% SKU delist, precision fermentation cuts allergens 30%.

Health & Nutrition +8.9% to $1.0 billion ($200B wellness 7.5% CAGR Mintel). VitaPlant milks +16% volumes +22% revenues, +2.1 share to 11.3% vs. Oatly; FiberFit Bars +11% gut health, 60% Walmart; ProFuel Shakes +13% collagen beauty. APAC +15% Japan; North America +9%; EMEA +6%. $150M Nutrition 2.0 app/QR personalization +20% trial, pea vertical integration.

Q4 4-6% organic, Beverages holiday lead, $300M productivity for 200 bps EBITDA expansion FY25.

Fifth, reviewing EPS guidance and key assumptions. For fiscal 2024, raising adjusted EPS to $4.85-$5.05 from $4.60-$4.85, 8-13% growth over 2023's $4.42 on Q1 strength (6.2% organic, 210 bps gross expansion), moderating inflation, FitFuture productivity. Adjusted excludes restructuring/M&A from PureHarvest.

Stable macro, 2.5% CPI, discretionary softness like Mondelez/Kellogg. Net sales 5-7%, organic 5.5% midpoint: 2% volume (AquaSpark +12% vs. 4% Nielsen), 2.5% pricing, 1% mix (premium 35% from 28% like PepsiCo). North America (65%) mid-single, beverages +3% volume, away-home -1%; EMEA (20%) low-single HFSS/UK Germany countered by GreenLeaf +15% Tesco; APAC/LatAm (15%) double-digit India mango Spark +18%, Brazil e-com +10% vs. Ambev.

Gross 48.5-49.5%, +100 bps: $180M FitFuture (AI manufacturing +5% yield), sugar hedged $0.18/lb from $0.22, cocoa $4200/ton capped, dairy/corn 2-3% vs. 7%; premium mix. SG&A 18-19% flat, $50M digital/trade; op profit 9-12%, margins +80-100 bps to 16.5%. Interest $120M (LIBOR+175bps $2.5B loan), tax 22%, shares 285M post $400M buybacks ($1B auth).

Risks: FX shave 1-2% (35% intl), low-income volumes, private label Walmart/Costco; moat 25% functional water share, NPS 72. 12-15% ROIC funds 10% dividend to $1.24, RTD coffee M&A like Celsius. Confident execution.

Sixth, analyzing organic revenue growth overall and by region. Q3 organic revenue growth 6.1%, ahead of 4-5.5% guide, third acceleration quarter. Pricing 3.4 points (lapped softer comps, 4-6% on 70% SKUs vs. cocoa/dairy/palm), volume/mix 2.7 points (1.9% volume, 0.8 premium/health). Beats industry 3.2%, Mondelez 4.9%, Hershey 2.1%; excludes 1.2pp FX, bolt-on yogurt.

North America (52%) 7.8%, almond-protein RTD triple-digit Northeast/Midwest velocity ($12B plant-milk 11% CAGR), low-sodium kettle +5% to 92% club, pricing +4.2 vs. Walmart/Aldi; e-com 18% +300bps Amazon/Instacart, 22% margin premium.

EMEA (28%) 4.9%, pricing +3.9 vs. Lidl/Aldi, mix +1.1 high-protein yogurt +15% UK/Germany (9% Kantar), volume +0.1 offset France, +1200 convenience SKUs; recyclable kids' pouches EU Green Deal.

APAC (15%) 9.2% from 7.1%, China oolong RTD +22% ($25B tea 12%), India savory +18% masala JioMart +400bps vs. Haldiram; Vietnam $50M coconut plant 15% superfruit CAGR; pricing +4.1 SE Asia palm.

LatAm (5%) 5.6%, pricing +4.8 tiered Brazil/Mexico 20% inflation (Coke playbook), volume +0.8 quinoa bars urban wellness; 85% FX hedge, 70% local corn.

15% SKU rationalization since 2022, 25+ annual launches 60% adjacencies, R&D 2.8% sales 3x ROI, Palantir AI forecast 92% accuracy -25% stockouts. Q4 5.5-6.5%, FY 5.8%, mid-single decade amid 7% premium CAGR, $600B snacking TAM.

Seventh, examining progress on sustainability initiatives and goals. Sustainability drives value: $150 million savings last year, 12% premium SKUs sales lift to 5% organic amid 78% Nielsen shopper shift, EU CSRD. Pillars: Planet, People, Prosperity.

Planet: 50% Scope 1/2 GHG cut by 2030 (2019 base), Q2 28% YoY to 1.2M tons CO2e; 65% manufacturing renewable (42% last), solar Juarez like Coke Ørsted PPAs. Scope 3 15% cut to 8.5M tons, 85% Tier 1 suppliers. Water intensity -22% to 1.8 m3/ton >20% goal; Central Valley almonds drip/regenerative 45k ha +35% yield -18% water, Almond Board. 92% beverages recycled/bio PET like Danone.

People: 96% priority commodities responsible (+8pp), 100% Rainforest cocoa HarvestChoc, 98% RSPO palm NDPE, 94% coffee 4C/Fair Trade IBM trace. Europe 99% EUDR, North America 95%, APAC 92% training 20k Indonesia/Vietnam farmers. Regenerative 120k acres +12% soil carbon like General Mills, vs. 10-20% yield loss WRI 2050.

Prosperity: 89% packaging diversion, 75% recyclable/compostable/reusable pre-SEC rules. Aluminum AquaSparkle -40% plastic, paper snack multipacks -55% virgin fiber; GreenHarvest 14% sales lift 22% $25B plant-based Euromonitor. 72% zero-waste sites (55%) $45M recycling. $300M next 3 years enzymatic Carbios, SAP AI for net-zero 2045.

Sustainability premiums +300 bps Q2 margins, hedges $2-3B carbon taxes Deloitte; ahead Unilever renewable, par Nestlé sourcing for BlackRock $10T ESG. El Niño palm +10% hedged/farmer premiums. H2 5-7% emissions via Brazil electrification/U.S. insets. 2030: 50% emissions, 100% sourcing, 2.0 m3/ton water.

Eighth, considering performance in key channels: retail, foodservice, convenience. Channels drove 8.2% organic net sales vs. 4.1% F&B IRI amid 6-8% CPG costs corn syrup/aluminum, premium mix.

Retail (52%) 7.5% organic + from Q1 5.2%, volume +2.8% first positive Q4'23, +1.9 velocity HydroSpark/NutriCrunch 120 bps $28B healthy share. +4200 ACV to 92% U.S. Kroger/Albertsons, Costco 12% 40-oz packs. Pricing +4.7 price/mix, trade 14.5%. North America 9.2% at-home +3% IRI; Europe 4.1% UK Aldi/Lidl rPET +15% Lidl; APAC China Tmall 18% kombucha. Snack Smart Walmart end-caps, AI planograms +10-15% facings.

Foodservice (28%) 6.8% strongest 2 years, volume +1.2% Circana away-home +4.5%. QSR +11% Sysco/US Foods ZestEnergy 2500 McDonald's/Taco Bell; Starbucks protein +15%. U.S. 8.4% labor menu simplify; LatAm Brazil 14% Habib's fruit waters; EMEA 2.1% Germany energy, Deliveroo ghosts. Operator Edge waste -8% Chipotle, heat-stable R&D; trade 16% loyalty.

Convenience (20%) 12.4% standout, volume +5.2% NACS U.S. traffic +7%. Impulse ZestEnergy/CrunchBites +3.1 velocity 250 bps $12B energy/snack; 85% ACV 7-Eleven/Circle K 12-oz iced teas 25% repeat. U.S. 14.2% Pilot; India Reliance 22% electrolytes; Canada 7% vape adjacents. IRI C-Store tweaks, Fuel Your Day displays +18% basket, Bumpers digital; compostable +30% pilots.

H2 retail mid-single, foodservice low-double, convenience 10-12% vs. 3-4% food-away inflation; 52% gross +110 bps pricing power. $150M capex aseptic, blockchain Nestlé-style, Instacart e-com; private label 22% vs. branded 18%, 5 new SKUs. Diversification outperforms bifurcated industry.

Overall, we are confident in our ability to navigate the current environment and deliver long-term value for our shareholders.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Sarah Jenkins to provide more detail on our financial results.

Sarah Jenkins (CFO):
Thank you, Johnathan. As Johnathan mentioned, we achieved solid results in Q3 2024. Net sales were $4.8 billion, representing a 7.2% increase year-over-year. Gross margin was 38.4%, impacted by input cost inflation partially offset by productivity savings and premium mix. Operating income was $512 million, and earnings per share were $1.12. We are managing our costs effectively and continue to invest in key growth initiatives.

Our balance sheet remains strong with $1.2 billion in cash and marketable securities. We are committed to returning value to shareholders through dividends and share repurchases.

For the full year, we are reaffirming our guidance for organic sales growth of 5% to 7% and adjusted EPS of $4.85 to $5.05.

Now, let's open the call for questions.

Operator:
Ladies and gentlemen, at this time we will begin the question-and-answer session. [Operator Instructions] Our first question comes from David Lee with Goldman Sachs. Please proceed.

David Lee (Goldman Sachs):
Good morning. Can you provide more color on the impact of recent inflation on your business?

Johnathan Hale (CEO):
Good morning, David. Inflation remains a key headwind, particularly in commodities like cocoa up 45% quarter-over-quarter and freight 22% above 2019 levels. In North America, it drove consumer downtrading with snack volumes down 1.2%, requiring elevated trade spend at 14% of sales. We've mitigated through hedging 85% of FY25 needs, $45 million Supply Chain Resilience savings, and targeted pricing contributing 2.8% to organic growth. Our premium Health & Wellness shift, now 28% of sales, provides margin resilience as consumers prioritize functional over value plays.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Emily Chen with Morgan Stanley. Please proceed.

Emily Chen (Morgan Stanley):
What are your plans for the new zero-sugar functional beverage line and what is the expected revenue impact?

Mike Thornton (Chief Growth Officer):
Thanks, Emily. Our zero-sugar electrolyte line, partnering with fitness influencers targeting Gen Z, is a cornerstone of Q4 innovation, building on NutriFlow's 12% volume growth. Plans include national rollout to 85% ACV in convenience and e-com to 18% penetration, with early tests showing 15% velocity like our air-fried crisps. Expected impact: 1-2 points to Q4 volume/mix, contributing to 4-6% organic guide, and accelerating Health & Wellness to 12% FY25 growth amid 11% sports drink category expansion per IRI. This positions us against Celsius-like trajectories in the $50 billion energy space.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Robert Kline with JPMorgan. Please proceed.

Robert Kline (JPMorgan):
How are you managing supply chain disruptions?

Lisa Chen (Chief Supply Chain Officer):
Robert, thanks for the question. Disruptions like Red Sea rerouting and West African cocoa shortages added $12 million to COGS, but our Resilience 2.0 initiative delivered $45 million savings via AI SAP forecasting—cutting inventory 18%, stockouts to 2%, delivery to 97%. We've nearshored 70% LatAm corn, vertical pea protein, hedged 85% commodities, and localized like sorghum in Brazil. Regional plants like Vietnam coconut support APAC 9.2% growth. Digitization and regenerative pilots on 120k acres build resilience against 10-20% climate yield risks per WRI.

Operator:
Our last question comes from Sophia Patel with Bank of America. Please proceed.

Sophia Patel (Bank of America):
What is your outlook for the rest of the year?

Sarah Jenkins (CFO):
Sophia, our outlook remains confident with Q4 organic 4-6%, FY24 5-7% at midpoint 5.5%, EPS $4.85-$5.05 on 48.5-49.5% gross margins via $180 million productivity, moderating 2-3% commodity inflation. Channels balanced: convenience 10-12%, retail mid-single; regions APAC/LatAm double-digit. Risks like FX or tariffs monitored, but $1.2 billion cash, ROIC 14% enable execution amid premium trends.

Operator:
I would now like to turn the call back over to Johnathan Hale for closing remarks.

Johnathan Hale (CEO):
Thank you for your questions and your continued interest in NutriCorp Foods. We are focused on executing our strategy and delivering strong results. We look forward to updating you on our progress next quarter.

Operator:
This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect.
